subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw's native backup CLI add gitignore-style exclusions now, and which defaults, auto-loaded files, and protected-path rules are acceptable for restore-critical and sensitive data?
rationale: The request changes a core recovery and security command; automation should not choose backup scope defaults, protected restore paths, or fail-open/fail-closed behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow and review the native PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288` into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep this issue open as a product backlog item and direct users to Keep My Claw or manual cleanup until maintainers are ready to own the core CLI surface.

options.title: Reject native scope
options.body: Close only after maintainers decide fine-grained filtering belongs outside core and document the supported ClawHub/plugin alternative plus its security tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review the native PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288` into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main backup CLI and archive-path history makes this the best available routing candidate, with the original and refactor authors as supporting context.
